cards.a: Large vesicles with many different jobs.
Collect extra water and pump it out of the cell.

cards.q: Why do freshwater protists like Paramecium need contractile vacuoles?
cards.a: Water keeps flowing in; without pumping it out, the cell would swell and burst.

cards.q: What do some vacuoles in plants and fungi do?
cards.a: Digest material, like lysosomes do in animal cells.

cards.q: What do small vacuoles in seeds store?
Why do flower petal vacuoles have pigments?
How can vacuoles protect a plant from animals?
cards.a: They store poisonous or bad-tasting chemicals, like nicotine and caffeine.

cards.q: How does the central vacuole help a plant cell grow?
cards.a: It soaks up water and gets bigger, enlarging the cell.

cards.q: What else does the central vacuole store?
cards.a: Important chemicals and toxic wastes - a safe trash can.

cards.q: Is a food vacuole part of the endomembrane system?
cards.a: Yes. It forms by pinching in from the plasma membrane, which is part of the system.
